role: Provider Partnerships Leader (backed by Y Combinator, $5M+ ARR, $20M+ raised)

hero.label: Made for Provider
hero.headline: I want to help Provider build the partnerships layer that scales healthcare.
hero.subheadline: Provider is solving a real coordination problem in healthcare, and you are doing it at a moment when the market is finally ready to move. I come from the outbound and relationship-building trenches, and I want to help you bring more providers into the network before your competitors figure out what you already know.

whyCompany.title: Y Combinator-backed healthcare infrastructure at exactly the right inflection point
whyCompany.body: Reaching $5M+ ARR with $20M+ raised means Provider has found real product-market fit and is now ready to scale partnerships in a structured way. That transition from scrappy early traction to repeatable growth is where a dedicated partnerships hire makes the biggest difference. I want to be that hire.

whyCompany.title: Early enough to shape the playbook, big enough to have real resources
whyCompany.body: Most startups at this stage are still figuring out whether the model works. Provider has already answered that question and is now asking how fast it can grow. Joining now means I get to help build the provider partnerships motion from the ground up, not inherit someone else's spreadsheet.

whyCompany.title: I have already done the hard version of this job in two different contexts
whyCompany.body: At Copygen.ai I ran cold outreach end to end and helped bring in 15 to 20 paying clients using HubSpot and LinkedIn sequences, which is exactly the outbound muscle provider partnerships requires. At NextAfter I moved into a more strategic B2B consultancy environment where I learned how to build trust with stakeholders over longer cycles. This role sits right at the intersection of those two experiences.

quote: Healthcare coordination is broken because the relationship layer was never built properly. I have spent the last two years learning how to open doors and keep them open, and I want to spend the next chapter doing that for Provider, where it actually matters.
